text_blocks.snippet: Doctors diagnose type 2 diabetes using specific blood tests that measure your average or current blood sugar levels.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests that measure your average or current blood sugar levels

text_blocks.snippet: You are diagnosed with type 2 diabetes if your test results meet any of these thresholds:

list.snippet: A1C Test: 6.5% or higher on two separate tests. This test measures your average blood sugar over the past two to three months without requiring you to fast.
Fasting Plasma Glucose Test: 126 mg/dL or higher after fasting (no food or drink except water) for at least 8 hours.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: 200 mg/dL or higher at any time of day, paired with classic diabetes symptoms.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): 200 mg/dL or higher two hours after drinking a special sugary liquid.
